eq.enabledHint: Ten bands and a preamp, after ReplayGain and before the volume.
eq.followHint: Switches to it while headphones are plugged in, as far as macOS can tell (Bluetooth headphones may count as speakers).
eq.preampHint: Presets set it so their boosts don't clip; lower it if you boost bands by hand.
effects.chorusAbout: Copies drifting slightly in pitch and time against the music, for a fuller, shimmering sound.
effects.echoAbout: Repeats that fade and darken, bouncing between the speakers as the spread rises.
effects.enabledHint: Turns the effects below on. Off, the music plays as it is, whatever they're set to; the same switch is in Features.
effects.flangerAbout: A sweeping, jet-like whoosh: a comb of notches moving through the sound.
effects.freezeAbout: Hold a moment of the music and sustain it as a drone, under the music or instead of it. The next track lets go.
effects.freezeOff: Switch the freeze on to hold.
effects.hint: Changes are heard as you move a control, and saved when you let go. While the freeze is on, the snowflake in the player bar holds the sound too.
effects.holdHint: Captures the sound playing now and sustains it.
effects.lofiAbout: Fewer bits and a lower sample rate, gritty and aliased like an early sampler.
effects.mixHint: How much of the effect you hear against the music.
effects.phaserAbout: Soft notches drifting up and down the spectrum.
effects.presetHint: Replaces every effect's settings with the preset's.
effects.reverbAbout: A room around the music: its size sets how long it rings, the damping how soon the highs fade.
effects.tremoloAbout: The level rising and falling, or, with stereo up, the sound moving from speaker to speaker.

favourites.title: Favourites
feature.classicalAbout: Groups movements under their work on album pages, adds Composer and Work to browsing, and shuffles a work as one.
feature.cueSheets: Cue sheets and chapters as tracks
feature.cueSheetsAbout: A single-file album with a cue sheet, or a file with chapters, becomes a track per cue or chapter. Changing this reads every file again.
feature.healthReportAbout: Finds files that don’t decode or are cut short, suspected lossy transcodes, albums whose tags disagree, and likely duplicates.
feature.libraryRadioAbout: “Start radio” in a track’s menu plays tracks like it from your library (genre, era, label, related artists), each saying why it was picked.
feature.listeningHistoryAbout: Remembers what you play (once half a track, or four minutes, has played), on this computer only.
feature.loudnessAnalysisAbout: Measures every track’s loudness in the background (EBU R128), so ReplayGain evens out files without ReplayGain tags too. Your files aren’t changed. A large library takes hours of processor time, once.
feature.lyricsAbout: Shows lyrics from the tags or a .lrc file next to the track in the Now Playing view; synced lines follow the music and seek when clicked.
feature.matchSampleRateAbout: Switches the output device to each track’s sample rate when it offers it, so nothing is resampled. Output pauses briefly at such a switch, and other apps using the device change rate too.
feature.moreInGenreAbout: Five random albums sharing a genre with the album you’re looking at.
feature.onThisDayAbout: Albums first released on today’s date in earlier years, on the Home page.
feature.playbackPreferencesAbout: Your own rules per track or album, from its menu: skip it in album and shuffle play, never shuffle an album, a gain offset, trims.
feature.practiceModeAbout: A–B loops, and playing slower or faster without changing the pitch (or changing the pitch alone), from a button in the playing bar.
feature.radioAfterQueue: Keep playing when the queue ends
feature.radioAfterQueueAbout: Any queue carries on as radio from its last track.
feature.recentlyAddedAbout: The albums that came into the library last, on the Home page.
feature.recentlyPlayedAbout: What you played last, with plays from one album together. Needs the history.
feature.recommendationsAbout: “More like this” for tracks, albums and artists, and albums you might like on Home, from your library and what you play. Nothing leaves this computer.
feature.outsideRecommendationsAbout: Artists you don’t have, like the ones you play most: from ListenBrainz’s similar artists and MusicBrainz’s relations, shown on Home and in “More Like This” for an artist. Goes online.
feature.segueShuffleAbout: Tracks that run into each other (live albums, DJ mixes, concept albums) shuffle as one, in order. Needs the analysis.
feature.signalPathAbout: Clicking the format in the playing bar shows every step from the file to the speakers.
feature.themesAbout: Choose or edit the app’s look in Settings › Appearance. Off, the app uses its standard look.
feature.effectsAbout: Reverb, echo, chorus, a spectral freeze and more on whatever plays, set in Settings › Effects. They change what you hear, so they start off.
feature.topPlayed: Top 20 of a year or month
feature.topPlayedAbout: Your most played tracks, albums and artists, on the History page. Needs the history.
feature.waveformSeekBarAbout: Draws the track’s waveform in the seek bar, showing quiet intros, drops and hidden tracks. The playing track is measured for it even with the analysis off.
features.clearHistoryConfirm: Forget every play in the listening history? This can’t be undone.
features.crossfeedHint: Blends a little of each channel into the other, as speakers do, so hard-panned stereo is easier on headphones.
features.headphonesOnlyHint: While macOS says headphones are plugged into this Mac. Bluetooth headphones can’t be told apart from speakers, so they need this off.
features.intro: Features beyond the usual. Each can be turned off; online ones and ones that listen on the network are off until you turn them on.
features.listenBrainzHint: Each play that counts is sent to your ListenBrainz account (a MetaBrainz service), with its MusicBrainz ids. Listens wait while you’re offline. Get your user token at listenbrainz.org › Settings.
features.outsideSent: Sent to ListenBrainz (labs.api.listenbrainz.org): the MusicBrainz ids of {artists}. Nothing else from your library or history leaves this computer.
features.outsideNothingSent: Nothing is sent yet: none of the artists you play most is matched to MusicBrainz.
features.portRange: The port must be a number from 1024 to 65535.
features.remoteHint: Serves a remote page to phones on this network (only local addresses are answered). A phone pairs once with a code shown here; forget it below at any time. macOS may ask to let the app use the local network.
features.skipSilenceHint: Jumps over a long silence inside a track (the gap before a hidden track), and ends a track in silence, after a few seconds of it. Needs the analysis.

playback.bufferHint: Smaller buffers respond sooner (pause, seek, the visualizer) but may crackle on a busy computer; larger ones are safer.
playback.crossfadeHint: Fades each track into the next. Never within an album, a work or tracks that run into each other, which stay gapless; nor between tracks at different sample rates.
playback.missing: {name} isn’t connected, so the default device plays; it takes over again when it’s back.
playback.now: Playing through {name} at {rate} kHz, {size} samples a block, about {latency} ms to the speakers.
playback.preampHint: Added to every tagged track’s gain. ReplayGain aims a little quieter than most modern releases.
playback.preventClippingHint: Turns a track up only as far as its tagged peak allows.
playback.rgAlbumAbout: Every album at about the same loudness, keeping the quiet and loud tracks within it.
playback.rgHint: Uses the ReplayGain (or Opus R128) tags that a loudness scanner such as foobar2000, beets or loudgain wrote into your files; they’re read when folders are scanned. A track with only one kind of gain uses that one in either mode.
playback.rgOffAbout: Every track plays as it was mastered.
playback.rgTrackAbout: Every track at about the same loudness; best for shuffle.
playback.untaggedHint: For tracks without ReplayGain tags, so they aren’t much louder than tagged ones.

updates.noRelease: No release has been published yet.

visualizer.calmHint: Calm mode: no pulses on beats, slower movement
visualizer.cantFollow: The visualizer can't follow the audio: {error}
visualizer.keys: Space plays or pauses · V changes the visualization · Esc leaves full screen
visualizer.noteText: Some visualizations pulse and flash in time with the music. Flashes are limited to three a second, and the picture dims if it flickers faster. If flashing light affects you, choose calm mode: no pulses on beats, and slower movement. Calm mode is also on whenever your Mac is set to reduce motion.
viz.bars.description: Bars from bass to treble, with falling peaks.
viz.bars.name: Spectrum
viz.covers.description: The covers of albums from the same year, or by the same artist, pulsing with the music.
viz.covers.name: Cover wall
viz.cymatics.description: Sand on a vibrating plate, gathering into the Chladni figure of the notes sounding: finer figures for higher notes.
viz.cymatics.name: Cymatics
viz.fifths.description: The notes sounding, around the circle of fifths, and the key the music seems to be in.
viz.fifths.name: Circle of fifths
viz.harmonograph.description: A pendulum drawing tuned to the interval between the two loudest notes: a fifth draws the 3:2 figure, a major third the 5:4.
viz.harmonograph.name: Harmonograph
viz.harmony.description: The pitch spiral beside the Tonnetz: the notes sounding, and the chords they make.
viz.harmony.name: Harmony
viz.kaleidoscope.description: The current cover, mirrored into a turning kaleidoscope that blooms with the music.
viz.kaleidoscope.name: Kaleidoscope
viz.portrait.description: The waveform plotted against itself a moment later, turning in three dimensions: a pure tone draws a ring, a rich timbre a knot, noise a cloud.
viz.portrait.name: Phase portrait
viz.recurrence.description: The track compared with itself as it plays: parts that come back, like choruses, light lines beside the diagonal.
viz.recurrence.name: Recurrence plot
viz.resonance.description: Cymatics with the phase portrait drawn over it: the figure of the notes, and the shape of their timbre.
viz.resonance.name: Resonance
viz.rhythm.description: Each bar a ring, one turn a bar, with the onsets marked where they fall, so a repeating rhythm lines up from ring to ring.
viz.rhythm.name: Rhythm rings
viz.ridges.description: The last few seconds of the spectrum as stacked ridges, like the cover of Unknown Pleasures.
viz.ridges.name: Ridgelines
viz.scope.description: The waveform as a glowing trace; each channel faintly behind their mix.
viz.scope.name: Oscilloscope
viz.spiral.description: Seven octaves of notes on a spiral, one octave a turn, so octaves share a spoke and harmonics make patterns.
viz.spiral.name: Pitch spiral
viz.stage.description: Where each sound sits between the speakers, bass at the bottom and treble at the top.
viz.stage.name: Stereo stage
viz.tonnetz.description: The harmonic lattice: fifths along each row and thirds up it, so every triangle is a chord, lit as it sounds.
viz.tonnetz.name: Tonnetz
viz.vectorscope.description: The stereo image: mono draws a vertical line, wide stereo a cloud; with the channels' correlation.
viz.vectorscope.name: Vectorscope
viz.vu.description: Analog meters with VU ballistics and peak lamps.
viz.vu.name: VU meters
vizOptions.calmHint: No pulses on beats and slower movement, for anyone affected by flashing light. Always on while macOS is set to reduce motion.
vizOptions.coverColoursHint: Otherwise every album gets the same colours.
vizOptions.cycleHint: Moves on to the next visualization while the visualizer shows.
vizOptions.frameRateHint: How often the sound is analysed.
vizOptions.sensitivityHint: Scales the spectrum: higher for quiet music, lower if the bars sit at the top.
vizOptions.visualizationHint: In the visualizer, V changes it.
welcome.drop: Or drag a folder onto this window. You can add more folders at any time.
welcome.lead: Add the folders your music is in. ano-mp reads them, never changes them, and keeps the library up to date as you add music.
welcome.listenbrainz: ListenBrainz is on: each track you listen to is sent there with your token.
welcome.never: Your files and their paths are never sent.
welcome.offline: Online sources are off: nothing leaves this computer.
welcome.onlineLead: To show covers, details and biographies, ano-mp asks these services about your music:
welcome.sends.coverArtArchive: the MusicBrainz release of each album, for its cover
welcome.sends.discogs: album titles and artist names, with your Discogs token
welcome.sends.musicbrainz: album titles, artist names and track lengths, to find each album and artist
welcome.sends.wikipedia: the names of Wikipedia articles MusicBrainz links to, for biographies
welcome.title: Welcome to ano-mp
